options: Encrypt values in a column
Perform calculations on a set of values to return a single summarised result
Split a table into multiple tables
Rename columns in a result set
Convert data types between text and numbers
questions.explanation: Aggregation functions perform calculations on a set of values to return a single summarised result, typically applied to database columns.

questions.stem: Instead of listing every employee's salary, what might an aggregation function be used to obtain?
options: Each employee's job title
The list of departments sorted alphabetically
The total salary expenditure for a department
The employee with the most recent start date
The number of columns in the employees table
questions.explanation: The example given is using an aggregation function to get the total salary expenditure for a department rather than listing each salary.

questions.stem: Which SQL aggregation function counts the number of rows in a result set?
options: SUM
AVG
MAX
COUNT
DISTINCT
questions.explanation: COUNT counts the number of rows, as in SELECT COUNT(*) AS TotalEmployees FROM employees.

questions.stem: Which SQL function computes the mean of values in a numeric column?
options: SUM
MIN
COUNT
HAVING
AVG
questions.explanation: AVG calculates the average (mean) of values in a numeric column, for example AVG(salary).

questions.stem: What does the SQL GROUP BY clause do?
options: Groups rows based on the values in one or more columns and applies aggregation functions to each group
Removes duplicate values from the result set
Sorts the result set in ascending order
Filters rows before aggregation
Joins two tables on a common column
questions.explanation: GROUP BY groups rows by specified columns so aggregation functions can be applied to each group, as in AVG(salary) per department.

questions.stem: What is the role of HAVING in a SQL query?
options: It selects the maximum value in a column
It filters the results of a GROUP BY based on a specified condition
It counts the rows in each group
It removes duplicate rows
It defines which table to query
questions.explanation: HAVING filters the results of a GROUP BY, for example HAVING AVG(salary) > 50000.

questions.stem: What does SELECT DISTINCT department FROM employees; return?
options: The number of employees in each department
The highest-paid department
The unique department values with duplicates removed
All departments including duplicates
The average salary per department
questions.explanation: DISTINCT removes duplicate values from the result set, so the query returns each department once.

questions.stem: Which query returns the lowest salary in the employees table?
options: SELECT MAX(salary) AS LowestSalary FROM employees;
SELECT AVG(salary) AS LowestSalary FROM employees;
SELECT COUNT(salary) AS LowestSalary FROM employees;
SELECT MIN(salary) AS LowestSalary FROM employees;
SELECT SUM(salary) AS LowestSalary FROM employees;
questions.explanation: MIN finds the minimum value in a column, so SELECT MIN(salary) returns the lowest salary.

questions.stem: What is described as the ultimate purpose of using aggregation functions?
options: To increase the number of rows in a table
To enforce referential integrity
To back up the database
To speed up inserts
To extract valuable insights from data by summarising it into a more manageable and interpretable view
questions.explanation: The ultimate purpose is to extract valuable insights, answering questions such as the average salary in a department or the number of orders in a month.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the common SQL aggregation-related functions and clauses listed?
options: MEDIAN
SUM
COUNT
GROUP BY
HAVING
questions.explanation: The listed items are COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX, GROUP BY, HAVING and DISTINCT; MEDIAN is not among them.
